text:
maya: Quick heads-up — vendor just sent a contract update for H200 batch. They bumped lead time for the remaining 12 units to 8–10 weeks and an 8% price uplift if we want air expedite. Also, 12 return units from the EU depot are stuck in FRA customs under an RMA hold. Need quick decision on split-commit + brokerage. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-2045

alex: ack. can you paste vendor note? does uplift apply per-PO or per-shipment?

maya: pasted key lines below from their email: "we can expedite 12 units via air (ETA 3–5 business days) at +8% unit price; remaining batch ships sea (ETA 6–9 weeks) at current price. Brokerage and customs handling fees apply to expedited airwaybills. 48h price lock available on air option."

jordan: on the RMA side — FRA broker says HS code mismatch on the commercial invoice, plus missing consignor EIN. that's why customs won't clear. current status: customs hold, broker requested corrected invoice + PLC.

ryan: cluster impact: if we lose those 12 H200s for 3–8 weeks capacity for eu-prod-dedicated will be short ~30% of peak for next 2 releases. we should consider temporary routing to us-west or reduce job batch sizes by 25% to avoid tail latency spikes.

alex: budgeting note — we can absorb +8% for 12 units if finance signs PO today. otherwise vendor withdraws 48h lock. we need a formal PO number. also ask: do we want to request vendor to include temporary loaners until replacements ship?

jordan: options from logistics: (1) pay brokerage (~€1,200) + correct invoice -> clear units in 48h; (2) reject and wait for sea shipment -> 6–9 weeks; (3) vendor split-ship: air expedite for 6 units now and 6 later to spread brokerage cost.

maya: my recommendation: accept air expedite for 12 units (approve +8%), cover brokerage to clear RMA, and lock remaining batch at current price sea-shipment. this minimizes SRE risk. cost delta calc: +8% * 12 = ~€45k uplift, brokerage ~€1.2k, net delta ~€46.2k.

ops-bot: Ticket OPS-2045 status updated -> with customs broker. Assigned: logistics/jordan.

alex: finance ok to fast-path PO if ops leads commit. @jordan can you confirm broker invoice and recipient contact? then I'll run /approve-po 9876 and ping finance.

jordan: broker asked for corrected invoice with our VAT and consignor address + AWB list. AWBs:```
12345678901
12345678902
12345678903
``` 
please supply the VAT number: DE123456789 and contact: "Depot FRA — Reception" <fra-depot@redwood.ai>

maya: confirming — approve air expedite +8% for 12 units, clear broker fee. alex — please run PO. ryan — can you kick the temporary routing plan to redirect non-latency critical workloads to us-west for next 3 weeks?

ryan: will put routing change in effect and post a short playbook in #eng-sre. low-risk jobs pool will shift, ETA 30m to change traffic.

alex: /approve-po 9876 -> finance notified. email to vendor sent copy to vendor-sales@helios.example with subject: PO#9876 — expedite 12 units at +8%. included LOE to cover brokerage.

jordan: broker confirmed they'll accept corrected invoice via email. sending now. once customs release we expect 24–48h final clearance.

maya: thanks. leaving note on OPS-2045 to track costs and mark rollback condition if vendor misses 48h lock. everyone add any final concerns here. :thumbsup:

alex: one ask — include clause for temporary loaners next time. vendor said they couldn't but will check.

jordan: update: broker uploaded manifest to portal, AWB 12345678901 shows status "with customs". I'll post final clearance time once it changes.

ops-bot: Reminder: please attach courier proof-of-delivery to OPS-2045 when release is complete.

maya: ack, thanks all. I'll update the runbook and schedule a short sync if clearance delays past 48h.
